description: Developing space mission game with unreal engine
summary: Our team developed an interactive Mars base simulator designed for young students interested in space exploration missions. Our goal is to make a accurate and easy to understand Mars game. We used Unreal Engine 5.8 and it's latest technologies for the game. The game includes real data from NASA sources like DONKI etc. it does not have unrealistic data. The game is easy to play and also explains every part on info panel. It is a top-down game and only requires mouse and E key to play. There is a power source, life supporter and research center in the game, they are all located in diffrent rooms of the map. Every room have their own interactions to keep the game interactive. The core gameplay loop revolves around in main computer, this computer manages all sources and actions in the space center. Every day another situation happens and the player have to decide what to do. At the end player required to collect 200 research points and the crew should be alive. All credits are avaliable at the end of the game.
details:
What It Does:
Our project is a 3D top-down Mars base simulator for young students who are interested in space exploration missions. The game takes place in Gale Crater in May 2024 (Sols 4184–4190). The base has three different rooms, Power Room, Life Support, and the Research Center. Each room has its own interactions and side quests. The main game loop runs on the main computer. Every day the computer uses real Mars weather and solar storm data from a JSON file, and the player has to make choices like charging the shields or continuing research. The player have to keep crew alive for 7 days. Also collect 200 research points.

Benefits:
By turning real events in NASA data into a playable game, students can actually understand what happens on Mars. We want to help students understand how space missions work in real world with using a game.

Tools, Software & Hardware Used

Engine & Code: Unreal Engine 5.8, C++ to read the JSON data and manage daily resources, Blueprints, and JetBrains Rider.

Data: Real NASA logs from Curiosity REMS and DONKI space weather archives (May 14–20, 2024).

Art & Assets: Modular Sci-Fi kits by Quaternius, Adobe Substance 3D Sampler for the Mars ground material, and UMG for the UI.

AI Tools: We used Google Gemini to generate the base Mars ground texture and Claude to help structure the NASA data scenarios and C++ subsystem under the hackathon time limit.

Hardware: Built with gaming laptop with an RTX 5070 GPU, 32 GB Ram, Ryzen AI7 350.

Creativity & Design Factors

No Fake Data: Instead of senfing random events, every temperature, solar flare, and communication blackout in our game actually happened on Mars in May 2024. Even Curiosity's broken wind sensor is included in the data.

Easy to Play: We kept the controls simple just the mouse and the "E" key and added clear info panels so anyone can play without getting confused.

Real Trade-offs: There is no single right answer in the game. If you push too hard for research points, the crew takes radiation damage. If you play based on staying healthy you run out of energy.
projectRefs: ApJ – CME impact at Mars, 17–18 May 2024
